items.question: How were the document embeddings evaluated for Wikipedia page classification, and what metrics were reported for that evaluation with LINE and the other methods?
items.gold_answer: All document vectors were used to train a one-vs-rest logistic regression classifier using the LibLinear package, with the labeled documents randomly split into training and evaluation sets. The reported metrics were Micro-F1 and Macro-F1, averaged over 10 different runs with different sampled training data.
items.evidence_quote: All document vectors are used to train a one-vs-rest logistic regression classifier using the LibLinear package 4.

items.question: Why does graph factorization outperform DeepWalk in the Wikipedia page classification results when compared with LINE-based methods?
items.gold_answer: Graph factorization outperforms DeepWalk because DeepWalk ignores the weights of the edges. The passage explicitly says this is the reason for the performance gap in the classification results.
items.evidence_quote: The graph factorization outperforms DeepWalk as DeepWalk ignores the weights of the edges.

items.question: Under what condition does LINE(1st+2nd) perform significantly better than all other methods, and what does this suggest about the two proximities in LINE?
items.gold_answer: When the supervised task allows concatenating the embeddings learned with LINE(1st) and LINE(2nd), the combined LINE(1st+2nd) method performs significantly better than all other methods. This suggests that first-order and second-order proximities are complementary to each other.
items.evidence_quote: As a result, the LINE(1st+2nd) method performs significantly better than all other methods.

items.question: How do the most similar words returned by LINE's first-order proximity differ from those returned by its second-order proximity in Table 4?
items.gold_answer: The second-order proximity returns words that are all semantically related, because it uses contextual proximity. In contrast, the first-order proximity returns a mixture of syntactically and semantically related words.
items.evidence_quote: We can see that by using the contextual proximity, the most similar words returned by the secondorder proximity are all semantically related words.
